hero.title: Driving Change in Canada's Trucking Industry
hero.subtitle: And we hope you will join us as we shape the future of trucking.
hero.body: The Women's Trucking Federation of Canada (WTFC) is a national non-profit advancing safety, opportunity, and inclusion across the trucking sector. We empower women, engage youth, and unite drivers, technicians, trainers, executives, and male allies to build a modern, resilient, and diverse industry. Since 2016, we've grown into a powerful network grounded in mentorship, advocacy, and real-world impact — because this is not just an organization, it's a community.

partners.title: Supporting women in trucking through quality products and resources
partners.footNote: WTFC partners are building a safer, more inclusive industry — with better PPE, stronger teams, and real accountability.

offer.title: Diversity that Delivers
offer.body: From mentorship to advocacy, from youth engagement to professional standards — our programs turn good intentions into measurable change across every level of the industry.

mentorship.title: Mentorship & Retention
mentorship.text: Paired with an experienced driver, mentor, or executive for at least six months. We have matched thousands of women with the people who keep them moving forward.

youth.title: Youth & Schools
youth.text: Careers in Motion brings WTFC into classrooms, giving students a real look at modern trucking — technology, logistics, and the people behind it.

advocacy.title: Advocacy & Policy
advocacy.text: We bring industry voices into the room on safety, fair opportunity, and the recognition of drivers as skilled professionals.

standards.title: Professional Standards
standards.text: A public campaign promoting respect, safe practices, and professional conduct on and off the road.

mission.title: Safety. Equity. Accountability. That's our road forward.
mission.body: The Women's Trucking Federation of Canada (WTFC) is building a stronger, safer, and more inclusive trucking industry. We champion women and underrepresented groups, expand career pathways, and advocate for drivers as skilled professionals who deserve respect, recognition, and safe working conditions.

items.elevate: Elevate Standards — modernizing training, credentialing, and professional development across the industry
items.safety: Promote Safety — leading public awareness campaigns and tackling the real-world safety challenges drivers face
items.community: Build Community — fostering mentorship, retention, and allyship across fleets, terminals, classrooms, and boardrooms

mission.closing: By uniting drivers, industry leaders, and allies, WTFC is reshaping Canadian trucking where equity, safety, and professionalism aren't goals, they're the baseline.

stats.title: A decade of measurable change
stats.footnote: Figures reflect WTFC programme reporting to date.

who.question: Who can join WTFC?
who.answer: Anyone who is positive and supportive of women in transportation. Despite the name, our membership is not limited to women — we welcome drivers, technicians, trainers, dispatchers, executives, students, and male allies. All board members volunteer their time.

national.question: Is WTFC national or provincial?
national.answer: National. WTFC operates across all Canadian provinces and territories, with chapters and volunteers in every region. Our programming — mentoring, youth outreach, safety campaigns, and events — runs coast to coast, and our career board lists roles nationwide.

training.question: Do you run driver training?
training.answer: We don't operate a driving school. What we do is raise standards: we promote industry training standards, advocate for recognized credentialing and professional development, and surface funded training programs (such as the Bredin Institute's equipment operator program) on our career board.

mentorship.question: How does the mentorship program work?
mentorship.answer: You tell us what you're aiming for. We match you with someone who has already walked that road — a driver, a technician, a trainer, or an executive — for a minimum six-month commitment. Mentors and mentees meet monthly, and members also get access to group workshops and networking events.

btb.question: What is "Bridging the Barriers"?
btb.answer: Our flagship annual conference. Bridging the Barriers brings together industry leaders, advocates, drivers, and professionals for a day of honest conversation, networking, and inspiration on breaking barriers and advancing the role of women in trucking. It runs in Ontario and Western Canada each year.

sponsor.question: How can my company support WTFC?
sponsor.answer: Corporate membership and sponsorship both work. Sponsorship funds our mentorship, youth, and safety programmes directly and earns your organization visibility with a national audience of transportation professionals. Visit our Impact page for tier details, or get in touch and we'll build something specific to your goals.

aboutPage.purposeBody: The Women's Trucking Federation of Canada is a non-profit organization established to encourage the employment of women in the Transportation Industry.
aboutPage.purposeBody2: Our purpose is to promote personal growth and responsibility whether you're "In the Office, under the Hood or behind the Wheel". Despite the name, our membership is not limited to women — we welcome anyone who is positive and supportive of women in transportation.
aboutPage.purposeBody3: We aim to provide a platform and open environment for women across the Transportation Industry to come together, problem solve, share ideas and help promote our industry to future generations as a viable career option.
